blocks.content: Universal adult franchise establishes political equality regardless of wealth, education, gender, or social status.

rows: Empowered youth by adding millions of new voters

items: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years; this is a frequently tested topic in UPSC and State PSC exams.
Article 326 directly relates to elections based on adult suffrage for the Lok Sabha and Legislative Assemblies.
Disqualification from voting is strictly limited to grounds specified under Article 326 or law enacted by Parliament.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 326 of the Indian Constitution guarantees elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies based on adult suffrage.
The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988, which came into force on March 28, 1989.
Universal Adult Franchise establishes true political equality, reinforcing the principle of 'one person, one vote, one value'.
Citizens can only be disqualified from voting on grounds of non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime, or corrupt/illegal practices as prescribed by law.
